# braidworks get

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cli_docs.py from `braidworks --help`; do not edit by hand.
     Run `make cli-docs` after changing the command line. -->

Look up --want for IDs (or --have TYPE=VALUE / --in-file), routing across sources. Also available as `braidworks weave`. For the task this serves, see the [how-to guides](../../how-to/).

```text
usage: braidworks get ID… --have TYPE --want TYPE[,TYPE…] [options]

Look up the --want types for each input, planning a route across the installed sources.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

inputs:
  ID                    values to look up, all of the type named by a bare --have TYPE.
  --have TYPE[=VALUE]   TYPE of the ID arguments, or a TYPE=VALUE input strand (repeatable;
                        broadcast onto every ID or --in-file row).
  --in-file PATH        batch input: a CSV/TSV with type-id columns, or (with --in-type) one value
                        per line. Use '-' for stdin.
  --in-type TYPE        treat --in-file as one VALUE per line of this strand type.

what to retrieve:
  --want TYPE[,TYPE…]   target strand types.
  --for-each RELATIONSHIP
                        fan the lookup THROUGH a relationship, then get --want for each result
                        (e.g. --for-each orthologs). Repeatable; implies --expand all.
  --traverse CAPABILITY
                        like --for-each but names a fan capability id directly (e.g. --traverse
                        ncbi.list_orthologs); the unambiguous form.
  --param NAME=VALUE    a capability parameter (repeatable); CAP:NAME=VALUE targets one step. See
                        `braidworks weavers` for each capability's parameters.

output:
  --format {human,json,jsonl,tsv,csv}
                        output format (default: human).
  --references          print source citations for the route to stderr.

Advanced: sources and routing:
  --only SOURCES        restrict to these source ids (comma/space separated).
  --policy {local_only,api_only,local_first,api_first}
                        backend policy (default: local_first).
  --expand none|all|top:K
                        fan out one→many set outputs (default: none, or all when --for-
                        each/--traverse is used).
  --max-expansion N     run-wide leaf limit (default: 10000); preserves all input roots and
                        reports omitted successors.

Advanced: review and exit status:
  --review-policy {halt,allow_continue,raise}
                        ambiguity/review policy (default: halt); allow_continue explicitly permits
                        candidate selection.
  --confidence-threshold 0..1
                        minimum confidence; lower results pause even with allow_continue.
  --strict              exit non-zero if any input is unresolved or needs review.

Advanced: cache, saved runs and archives:
  --cache-db PATH       opt-in local SQLite lookup cache.
  --cache-positive-ttl SECONDS
                        lifetime of found/ambiguous cache entries (default: 3600); 0 disables
                        caching them.
  --cache-negative-ttl SECONDS
                        lifetime of no-match cache entries (default: 300); 0 disables caching
                        them.
  --cache-max-bytes BYTES
                        cache payload budget (default: 256 MiB); the SQLite file size may differ.
  --run-db PATH         opt-in local saved-run store (makes this a resumable run).
  --run-id ID           name for the new saved run; existing IDs are never overwritten.
  --lease-seconds SECONDS
                        run owner lease, renewed while executing (default: 60).
  --archive PATH        save a self-contained JSON run archive (new file; no overwrite).

examples:
  braidworks get P04637 --have protein.query --want protein.name
  braidworks get P04637 TP53 --have protein.query --param organism=9606 \
      --want protein.name,structure.pdb.ids --format tsv
  braidworks get --in-file ids.txt --in-type protein.query --want protein.name
  braidworks get --have gene.ncbi.id=7157 --for-each orthologs --want gene.symbol
```
